title: Deployment Consent and Forensic Evidence Flow: Operational Assurance Playbook
author: Priya Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the end-to-end gating, logging, and forensic evidence orchestration requirements for production deployments that cross security, residency, or tenancy boundaries. It is intended for engineering release leads, SREs, security on-call, and compliance reviewers.

Goals
- Ensure every cross-boundary deployment has explicit consent and an auditable approval trail.
- Standardize RBAC checks, immutable audit logging, and evidence packaging for post-deploy forensics.
- Minimize legal/regulatory exposure for deployments that touch restricted datasets or regions.

Scope
- Applies to: model and runtime releases, configuration rollouts, major infra changes, and migrations that impact data residency, tenant isolation, or privileged entitlements.
- Excludes: incremental non-privileged config flags that do not change residency or access boundaries (see Exceptions section).

Definitions
- Deployment consent: Formal approval combining RBAC authorization, security signoff, and residency acceptance recorded in the approvals registry.
- Evidence bundle: A time-bound, signed archive containing logs, entitlement snapshots, config manifests, and cryptographic markers used for audits.
- Cross-boundary: Any change that moves data, execution, or access across region/tenant/legal boundaries.

Owners and Roles
- Release Lead (owner): Coordinates approvals, ensures checklist completion, owns evidence handoff.
- Security Reviewer (security): Validates access changes, RBAC role mappings, KMS usage, and residency constraints.
- SRE / Operations (eng-sre): Validates observability hooks, audit-forwarding, and rollback readiness.
- Compliance (finance-legal/compliance): Validates retention and evidence packaging meets regulatory scope.
- On-call Incident Responder (security/eng-sre): Executes forensic collection in incidents and validates bundle provenance.

Pre-deployment Requirements (must be satisfied prior to gating)
1) RBAC gating
   - All privileged role changes must be scoped to a timebound approval (JIT or ephemeral) and recorded in the approvals registry (service: authz-service).
   - Entitlement diffs are required: produce 'entitlement-snapshot.json' showing before/after bindings for affected principals.
   - Approvals must reference a runbook ID and include at least one security reviewer and one service owner.

2) Audit-logging and observability
   - Audit-collector must be live and ingesting for the target region prior to deploy.
   - Required event types: AUTHZ_DECISION, TOKEN_ISSUE, SVC_DELEGATION, DEPLOY_START, DEPLOY_COMPLETE, CONFIG_CHANGE.
   - Log retention policy: minimum 180 days for AUTHZ_DECISION and CONFIG_CHANGE events for deployments touching regulated tenants.

3) Data residency and retention checks
   - Confirm data flow diagrams for the release: list of storage endpoints and their residency labels (e.g., us-west-2, eu-central-1, customer-ssa).
   - If new endpoints are introduced, obtain residency acceptance signoff from legal/compliance.

4) Secure SDLC gating
   - The release must pass the security gate in CI (static analysis, dependency provenance, signed artifacts).
   - Build artifacts must be signed with the org's CI key and verification recorded in the approvals registry.

Consent-to-Deploy Checklist (must be recorded in the approvals registry)
- [ ] Release notes and impact matrix uploaded to releases-service with release-id.
- [ ] RBAC entitlement-snapshot attached.
- [ ] Security reviewer approval (signed).
- [ ] Residency acceptance (if applicable).
- [ ] Audit-collector warm: test events observed within 5 minutes.
- [ ] Evidence collection plan attached (who, where, retention).
- [ ] Rollback trigger points defined (latency, error-rate, cost, privacy).

Runtime Controls and Thresholds
- Latency SLO impact: If p95 latency increases by >20% for fronting routes, auto-hold the deployment.
- Error spike: If 5xx rate exceeds 1% for 5 consecutive minutes, auto-rollback.
- Data egress: Any outbound transfer to a new country must pause deployment until residency approval is confirmed.

Incident Response: Forensic Evidence Collection Steps
1) Triage and preserve
   - Immediately set the deployment to 'paused' and capture the current deployment commit ID.
   - Signal audit-collector to snapshot logs for the impacted window (service: audit-edge-snapshot).

2) Snapshot entitlements and keys
   - Run: curl -s https://authz-service/api/v1/entitlement-snapshot?deploy=<id> > entitlement-snapshot.json
   - Record active KMS key IDs used for signing and encryption in 'key-manifest.txt'.

3) Evidence bundle assembly (immutable, signed)
   - Bundle contents (mandatory): entitlement-snapshot.json, deployment-manifest.yml, audit-logs-window.jsonl, metrics-window.prom, key-manifest.txt, approvals-registry-export.json, and CI-artifact-signature.sig.
   - Use 'evidence-pack' tool to create a signed bundle: evidence-pack --input <files> --sign-with /etc/ci/keys/release-key.pem --output evidence-<deploy-id>.tar.gz.sig
   - Store the sealed bundle in evidence-bucket/evidence-<deploy-id>.tar.gz.sig with object immutability TTL = 365 days (for regulated tenants).

4) Handoff and analysis
   - Notify security@redwood with: deploy id, bundle S3 path, snapshot timeframe, and summary of suspected impact.
   - Compliance will schedule evidence review within 3 business days for high-severity incidents; otherwise within 10 business days.

Evidence Packaging and Provenance Requirements
- Every evidence bundle must include: who created it (principal), ISO8601 timestamps, signer fingerprint, and a provenance.json containing the SHA256 of each included object.
- Cryptographic markers: sign bundles with CI release key and record signature in approvals-registry. Verify signatures during audits.
- Tamper-evidence: Enable server-side object lock and versioning on S3 evidence buckets.

Data Residency Handling in Evidence
- When evidence contains personal or regionally-sensitive data, produce two variants: 
  - Redacted bundle for broad internal review (PII redacted, redaction list recorded),
  - Full bundle stored with restricted access controls and legal hold.
- Cross-border transfer of full bundles is prohibited without documented legal exception. See Exceptions section.

RBAC and Entitlement Forensic Patterns
- Snapshot format: JSON array of bindings with fields [principal, role, resource, scope, timestamp, changed_by, approval_id].
- Expect to capture: temporary tokens (mask secrets), delegated sessions, and JIT grants associated with the deployment window.
- Correlate AUTHZ_DECISION logs with the entitlement snapshot to prove whether a given decision was authorized by the recorded bindings.

Risk and Exception Handling
- Low-risk exceptions (e.g., emergency patch to non-regulated tenant) can be fast-tracked: must be approved by the on-call security lead and flagged in the approvals-registry within 24 hours.
- High-risk exceptions (changes that alter residency or elevate privileged entitlements) require executive signoff and creation of a timebound mitigation plan before any cross-border data movement.
- Each exception must capture: rationale, compensating controls, expected duration, rollback criteria, and owner.

Operational Runbook Snippets
- Force-create entitlement snapshot (CLI):
  $ redwood-authz snapshot --deploy-id $DEPLOY_ID --output entitlement-snapshot.json

- Trigger audit-edge snapshot (API):
  POST https://audit-collector.internal/api/v1/snapshot
  Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN
  Body: {"start":"2026-08-12T13:00:00Z","end":"2026-08-12T13:20:00Z","reason":"deploy-triage","target":"us-west-2"}

Appendix: Minimal Evidence Schema (human readable)
| field | description | example |
| deploy_id | unique deployment identifier | release-2026-08-12-37 |
| created_by | principal who assembled bundle | ci-service-account@redwood.internal |
| signature | base64 signature of archive | XJ3k... |
| items | list of included filenames and SHA256 | ["entitlement-snapshot.json:abc123"] |

Related tools and services
- authz-service (entitlement registry and JIT), audit-collector (log ingestion + snapshot api), evidence-pack (bundle & sign), approvals-registry (consent records), releases-service (release metadata), kms (key manifesting).

Frequently Asked Questions
- Q: Can a deployment proceed with an unresolved residency question?
  A: No — any unresolved residency acceptance pauses the deployment until compliance/legal signoff, unless a documented emergency exception is approved.

- Q: How long are evidence bundles retained?
  A: Default retention is 365 days. For regulated tenants or open investigations, retention is extended per legal hold.
